title: Freya and the Current
premise: Elodie Dravenmoor's salvage crew is hired to recover equipment from a wrecked survey vessel on the Kestrel River, a waterway closed under a mining concession nobody will name. When they find the expedition's radio log instead of wreckage—recordings proving the company drowned its own survey team to bury contamination evidence—the crew becomes a liability marked for erasure. Hunted by concession security and betrayed by their own financier, Elodie and her ragtag divers must carry the recordings over the Serrat Range before first snow seals the passes and before the permits expire, which would legally erase the crime along with its witnesses. They lose two of their own and nearly their humanity to get through, but Elodie broadcasts the log from a ranger station at the summit as the snow falls, forcing an inquiry that finally drags the company into daylight.
about_author: Ansel Quintana is the pen name of a former maritime salvage hand who spent six seasons working rivers no map bothered to name. He writes adventure fiction about people the law forgot, from a cabin he refuses to geotag.

chapters.title: Cold Water Rules
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Her crew finishes a routine hull salvage when a navy patrol boat shadows them off the Kestrel delta without explanation. Introduces the crew: gruff engineer Tam, young diver Sef, navigator Ilsa. Emotional beat: unease beneath competence—the wilderness is watching them back.

chapters.title: The Contract Nobody Signs
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A fixer named Corvan offers triple rates to recover 'survey equipment' from a wreck upriver, with clauses forbidding photography or radio disclosure. Tam smells a trap; money talks. Emotional beat: temptation versus instinct, the crew voting yes for reasons each keeps private.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The journey into the concession zone: burned checkpoints, a river running strangely milky, villages emptied by buyouts. Sef finds a child's boot in the shallows. Emotional beat: creeping dread as the landscape itself testifies to something wrong.

chapters.title: The Wreck That Wasn't Wrecked
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Diving the survey vessel, Elodie finds clean scuttle charges, not storm damage—and a sealed strongbox bolted below the waterline, deliberately hidden. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into certainty that someone wanted this ship sunk and its cargo lost.

chapters.title: Voices in the Box
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The strongbox holds a field recorder: radio logs of the survey team reporting catastrophic tailings contamination hours before the 'accident.' The last entry is screaming cut short. Emotional beat: horror and moral vertigo—they now hold proof worth killing for.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Concession security arrives by airboat, polite and armed, asking what they've recovered. Elodie lies smoothly; Tam realizes she's decided before telling anyone. Emotional beat: the crew's trust tested as they choose silence together without saying so aloud.

chapters.title: The Financier's Voice
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A satellite call reveals their employer Corvan has sold them out—the security detail was told to leave no witnesses. Ilsa hides the recorder inside a ballast tank. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into resolve; invisibility is over.

chapters.title: Night Run
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The crew scuttles their own boat to fake their deaths and slips into the flooded forest in a dive skiff. Security burns their camp behind them. Emotional beat: grief for the boat, terror and exhilaration of becoming ghosts.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Mile 40
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. They shelter with Old Vashti, a disgraced concession hydrologist living off-grid who confirms the contamination and knows the mountain trails. Emotional beat: unexpected kindness; belonging found in another exile.

chapters.title: What Vashti Knows
chapters.summary: Vashti's POV. She explains the permits expire at first snow, after which the concession legally resets and all records within it become company property. The recordings must reach the mining registry office beyond the range—or vanish forever. Emotional beat: the stakes crystallize into a deadline written in weather.

chapters.title: Provisions and Promises
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Resupply raid on a concession depot goes wrong; Sef is shot in the shoulder covering their retreat. Emotional beat: guilt and fury—Tam carries Sef while questioning whether justice is worth other people's blood.

chapters.title: The Ascent Begins
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The crew enters the Serrat foothills with Vashti guiding, pursued by tracker teams and racing a cold front. Emotional beat: grim determination, the group forging into terrain where mistakes are fatal and mercy is expensive.

chapters.title: Whiteout Camp
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Storm traps them for two days above the treeline; food runs low and Sef's wound turns septic. Tam confesses his criminal past and why he owes Elodie. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in misery, secrets spent like currency.

chapters.title: The Pass of Names
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Delirious, Sef narrates crossing a pass littered with cairns left by previous expeditions that never came back—including, they realize, the survey team's escape attempt. Emotional beat: communion with the dead, resolve hardened by their failure.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Col
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Security catches them at the high col. In the firefight, Vashti takes a bullet meant for Elodie and stays behind with a rifle to hold the narrows. Emotional beat: sacrifice without ceremony; the cost of the truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Descent Into the Company Town
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Wounded and starving, they descend toward Registry only to find the town locked down under company martial law ahead of permit expiry. Emotional beat: despair at the machine's reach—justice has a front door, and it's barred.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A registry clerk, Maren, whose brother died on the survey vessel, agrees to help but warns the official channel is compromised. Emotional beat: fragile hope—an ally inside the walls, and the discovery that corruption has limits after all.

chapters.title: Deadline Dawn
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Permits expire at noon; security sweeps the town. The crew splits: Tam creates a diversion at the fuel depot, Ilsa and Sef carry the recorder to the old ranger station with a functioning transmitter on the ridge. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the transmitter, Elodie reads the survey logs live across every emergency band as security breaches the station. Tam's fire covers their escape down the scree. Emotional beat: triumph and terror braided—the truth is loose and cannot be recalled.

chapters.title: The Long Fall
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The descent through falling snow, evading searchlights, carrying Sef. News crackles on a stolen radio: the broadcast reached a federal judge; the registry is sealed pending inquiry. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Weeks later, depositions in a coastal city; Corvan arrested, the concession suspended, Vashti posthumously cleared. The crew stands awkward in clean clothes, out of their element. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, outside the law that failed them, yet through it anyway.

chapters.title: The Current Remembers
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Spring: the crew returns to the Kestrel to dive the wreck properly, recovering the survey team's remains for burial. Elodie leaves a cairn at Mile 40 for Vashti. Emotional beat: quiet belonging—the wilderness forgives nothing, but it keeps faith with those who keep faith with it.
